It is configured in three steps, in order. The field allowlist the rule engine already governs is reused, so a workflow may touch only what an operator has permitted.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wf1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Field Allowlist — shared with the rule engine, above. A field is read or written by a workflow only where it is listed for the matching grain. An unlisted field is refused at author time, so a column that was not permitted can never be touched.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wf2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Action Groups — a named, reusable bundle of actions: a field is updated, a task is created, a webhook is called, a message is sent. What each group reads from and writes to workflow state is declared on it. A group is authored once and referenced by many workflows; its actions are frozen into a workflow when that workflow is saved, so a later edit is adopted only when the workflow is re-saved.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wf3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Workflows — the graph itself: nodes (Step, Branch, Wait, Assign, Terminal) wired by their edges, scoped to a grain and an entry event. An immutable version is frozen on save, and a running instance stays bound to the version it began on, so an edit never disturbs a lead already in flight. Nothing is started until the workflow is enabled.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wfafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Once a workflow is enabled, an instance is created for each matching subject and advances on its own — waking on a timer, or when an external system delivers a signal. Its progress is shown below.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wfsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Action Groups", "col": 6}}, {"id": "wfsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Workflows", "col": 6}}, {"id": "wfsp2", "type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}}, {"id": "wfmonhdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Workflow Monitor", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wfmon", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Running Instances is the live queue — one row per lead, showing the node it rests at and whether it is running, parked, done, or failed. Signal Inbox holds the events delivered by external systems, each awaiting the instance that consumes it. Step Log records every node an instance has executed, for audit.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wfsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Running Instances", "col": 4}}, {"id": "wfsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Signal Inbox", "col": 4}}, {"id": "wfsc5", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Step Log", "col": 4}}]
